name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 partisan lean makes the district structurally Democratic
Grijalva's fundraising dominance: $2.5M to $232K raised and $469K to $12K cash on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 99%
No general-election polling, so the exact margin is uncertain
model.rationale: A D+13 district, a well-funded incumbent outraising her opponent by more than ten to one, and market pricing near certainty all point to a comfortable Democratic hold; the only real uncertainty is the size of the margin, since no public polls are available.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Grijalva or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though not enough to put the seat in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This heavily Democratic southern Arizona seat carries a D+13 partisan lean, and the incumbent holds every visible advantage. Adelita Grijalva has raised about $2.5 million to Republican Daniel Butierez's $232,000 and ends with a cash edge of roughly $469,000 to $12,000. Outside spending also runs heavily in her favor, with more than $380,000 supporting her against modest opposition. No public general-election polls track the race.

With polling absent, the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign resources, both pointing the same way. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 99 percent. Nothing in the evidence suggests an environment shift large enough to put the seat in play, and the Republican campaign's thin funding leaves little obvious path to competitiveness.
